alyssa: Quick sync — can we standardize span naming + semantic attrs for LLM requests? We're getting a bunch of variants across runtime/exporter/console and it's hurting dashboards + traces. cc @mike @priya
mike: Strong yes. Suggestion: keep span.name low-cardinality, e.g. `llm.request`. Put model name/version/variant in attributes, not in the span name. prevents name explosion in tracing UIs. :thumbsup:
priya: Agree on low-cardinality names. For debugging we should add a hashed model id attr (truncated) so we can correlate exactly which binary served the request without leaking too much card. e.g. `llm.model.id = sha256(model_binary)[0:12]`. Also propose `llm.model.variant` + `llm.model.quant` for quantization info.
darren: We also need per-op spans for cache and decode: `llm.cache.lookup` (fast, often), `llm.decode` (token generation), but those should be optional to emit depending on sampling. Main request span stays `llm.request`.
eva: Monitoring asks for tokens in spans. We rely on `tokens.input`/`tokens.output` for cost and latency splits. Proposal: attributes `llm.tokens.input`, `llm.tokens.output`, and `llm.tokens.total` (computed). Also `llm.cache.hit` boolean.
priya: One more: batch size and routing policy matter for perf. Add `llm.batch.size`, `llm.route.policy` (e.g., "latency", "cost", "isolation"), and `llm.device` (e.g., a100-v5).
mike: Concern: high-cardinality values like full model names or request prompt hashing in spans will blow up our traces. Keep those as attributes but only store them in sampled traces. For metrics/aggregates store lightweight labels: `model.family` (e.g., "mistral"), `model.size` (e.g., "7b").
alyssa: Good call. We should document which attrs are high-cardinality and behind sampling. Draft list in code block for engineers to copy into runtime: 
```
Span(name="llm.request", attributes={
  "service.name": "redwood-inference",
  "llm.model.family": "mistral",
  "llm.model.size": "7b",
  "llm.model.version": "v0",
  "llm.model.id": "sha1:abc123def456",
  "llm.model.variant": "base",
  "llm.model.quant": "q4_0",
  "llm.tokens.input": 12,
  "llm.tokens.output": 88,
  "llm.tokens.total": 100,
  "llm.cache.hit": false,
  "llm.batch.size": 1,
  "llm.route.policy": "latency",
  "llm.device": "a100-v5"
})
```
darren: We'll also add small op-level spans when sampling is enabled: `llm.cache.lookup` with `{ "llm.cache.hit": true/false, "llm.cache.type": "prefix" }` and `llm.decode` with `{ "llm.decode.tokens": 88, "llm.decode.ms": 120 }`. Keep those off by default to limit volume.
infra-bot: lint:otel_spans_check FAILED — span names found: `model.predict`, `llm.infer_call` — please rename to `llm.request` and include attributes per spec. See CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345
mike: I'll add a CI job that enforces allowed span names and required top-level attrs (model.family, model.size, tokens.total). Lint will error if missing.
alyssa: UX note — console rollouts page expects `model.family` + `model.size` to group metrics. That aligns nicely with low-cardinality attrs.
eva: Retention question: telemetry wants full-span retention for 30 days, aggregate metrics for 365. Is that ok?
priya: Works for ML — we store detailed sampled traces 30d, but we export metrics and counts (cache hits, token histograms) to long-term storage. Add explicit export mapping in docs.
mike: Action items:
- runtime: emit `llm.request` + attrs; add sampling flag to emit op-level spans (darren + runtime team)
- exporter: map attrs to metrics (tokens histogram, cache hit rate) and tag by `model.family`/`size` (mike)
- docs: update telemetry conventions doc + example code (alyssa)
- CI: add otel span checker rule (mike)
infra-bot: created task TKT-891 in eng-platform: "Implement LLM OTEL span conventions"
alyssa: Great. I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up if needed. Thanks everyone :rocket:
